column1: # Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity (Koei Tecmo's KTGL engine on NVN, SDK 9.6.0), update v327680 = 1.3.0.
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile; values marked "Mario's" are not measured for this game yet.
# RomFS: Koei Tecmo RDB archives (asset/*.rdb index + asset/*.rdb.bin* data, asset/data/*.file), a run of IDRK entries with zlib in chunks.
# The shaders are GLSLC compiler outputs: 118 in main and the rest in KTGL's G2S containers inside the RDB data files (shader_split.py idrk_shaders).
# subsdk0 is Nintendo's movie library (NintendoSDK_movie, as in Metroid Dread)
# The NPDM declares no system resource (META +0x14 = 0): the game uses SetHeapSize. Link's Awakening's partition until measured
# The game sizes its heap as total − used memory (nninitStartup, main+0x8ad318), and SetHeapSize must then fit beside the code: the three modules take 66.6 MB (68 MB rounded), more than the
# 64 MB the host reports by default. SetHeapSize(pool − 64 MB) failed with ResultLimitReached, AllocateMemoryBlock returned 0x1003, the game's malloc was never set up, the 866 MB
# graphics heap allocation failed (main+0x8aeb4c) and nnMain returned at once. 72 MB = the image plus stacks: the heap is 0xc8c00000 (3212 MB) and the game's fifteen sub-heaps (3098 MB) fit
# Movie frames (VP9, NV12 to a buffer): the game copies each frame into a 1280x720 R8 and a 640x360 RG8 texture in a CPU-visible pool and publishes them with
# nvnMemoryPoolFlushMappedRange; without the upload the intro movie stayed black under its "+ Skip" prompt
# The Switch version shows 30 fps and steps the game a fixed amount per update: a KIDS task waits out 1/30 s and steps the game clock by 1/30 s, the battle steps 1 / the game's frame-rate
# block (30.0), and the event scripts step by the KTGL device's frame rate (59.94 / present interval 2). On 1.3.0 main (patches.py FRAME_STEP) three stubs run the updates at the cap
# and set all three to it (with only a 1/60 s wait the clock and the battles ran at twice real time); the host paces the presents at 60 fps, 30 when 60 does not hold.
# The updates step by the cap whatever the hold, so holding late frames only paces the screen: frames are shown as soon as they are ready (the 60fps IPA ran battles at 45–57).
# The iPhone battle's GPU going from 10 to 41 ms a frame was first read as its GPU clock following the hold; the same rise came with no hold at all: the battle runs about 1,000 to
# 2,800 compute dispatches a frame after its first cutscene, which each had an encoder of their own (nvn_mtl.m dispatch_enc)
# KTGL binds whole mesh pools (up to ~590,000 vertices) and its soldiers' Half2 / Short2 attributes feed integer shader inputs, which the replay converts on the CPU:
# over the bound ranges that was millions of vertices a frame in battle (26 fps at any target on the Mac); only over the vertices each draw reads. Shadow vertex inputs
# (nvn_mtl.m vin_on) now take those attributes on the GPU; this still serves the draws that keep the CPU conversion (transform feedback, DM_NVN_VCONV_CPU=1)
